items.title: How Trump Is Dismantling America’s Scientific Research Machine
items.author: Christopher Flavelle, Irena Hwang, Adam Sella, Alan Blinder, Sheryl Gay Stolberg, Benjamin Mueller and Michael C. Bender
items.content: <article>The system that has driven life-altering discoveries and helped make the United States a superpower is now under intense strain.</article>

items.title: Trump’s Arch Faces New Legal Challenge From Virginia and D.C.
items.author: Luke Broadwater
items.content: <article>The two jurisdictions contend that President Trump’s proposed 250-foot arch is “flagrantly unlawful,” citing concerns over traffic, the environment and historic preservation.</article>

items.title: Susan Collins Is Always Keeping Score
items.author: Michael Kruse and Lisa Lerer
items.content: <article>The long-serving senator has delivered millions of dollars to every corner of her state. But in Maine, people say, it’s best to avoid getting on her bad side.</article>

items.title: Talarico Makes Final Election Pitch to Texans: ‘You Are My Slingshot’
items.author: Robert Draper
items.content: <article>The Democratic candidate for Senate has led in polls. But because it’s Texas, he remains the underdog.</article>

items.title: Pete Ricketts Leads Dan Osborn in Nebraska Senate Race, Poll Finds
items.author: Ruth Igielnik and Emily Davies
items.content: <article>Voters see Dan Osborn, the independent seeking to unseat Senator Pete Ricketts, as more like a Democrat than an independent, a Times/Siena poll found.</article>

items.title: Trump and GOP Close Midterms With Ugly Personal Attacks
items.author: Tim Balk and Sam Easter
items.content: <article>Facing backlash over inflation and anger with the president, Republicans have turned to an onslaught of baseless claims about Democratic candidates.</article>

items.title: In Nebraska Senate Race, the Independent May Have an Identity Problem
items.author: Nate Cohn
items.content: <article>Dan Osborn trails by six points, and voters don’t seem to buy that he’s truly independent from Democrats.</article>

items.title: As Midterms Near, Top Law Firms That Capitulated to Trump Are on the Sidelines
items.author: Michael S. Schmidt and Jim Rutenberg
items.content: <article>None of the firms that struck deals to avoid crippling executive orders are publicly involved in the major legal efforts to check the Trump administration’s attempts to meddle in the midterm elections, a review by The New York Times shows.</article>

items.title: A Halloween Tale: Ghost Stories of the U.S. Capitol
items.author: Olivia Diaz and Alex Kent
items.content: <article>The ghost stories, dating back to the 19th century, are fitting for a building where the past rarely stays dead.</article>

items.title: Voters Usually Ignore Corruption as an Issue. It Now Has Their Attention.
items.author: David Ovalle and Emily Cochrane
items.content: <article>Voters have shrugged off accusations of corruption for years, believing all politicians are corrupt, but thanks to President Trump’s unpopularity and growing wealth, the issue is breaking through.</article>

items.title: Justice Dept. Confirms Alaska Inquiry Even as Its Focus Remains Unclear
items.author: Anna Griffin and Glenn Thrush
items.content: <article>Democrats and former officials have accused the department of pursuing a political goal in the guise of a legal one: to publicize a scheme, sordid but not illegal under state law, damaging to Democrats.</article>

items.title: Judge Blocks Expediting Migrant Children’s Asylum Cases, For Now
items.author: Madeleine Ngo
items.content: <article>Lawyers for the children praised the pause on fast-tracked interviews of unaccompanied minors, calling it a blow against the Trump administration’s “deportation assembly line.”</article>

items.title: Alina Habba’s Husband Ignited Drama in Trump’s Circle. Now He’s Under Scrutiny.
items.author: Anatoly Kurmanaev, Tyler Pager and Declan Walsh
items.content: <article>Turhan Mildon, who married Alina Habba this summer, presents himself as a 29-year-old billionaire with ties to global leaders. His story has inconsistencies.</article>

items.title: Obamacare Policies Hit Again With Steep Premium Increases for 2027
items.author: Reed Abelson and Margot Sanger-Katz
items.content: <article>Premiums will increase an average 13 percent next year for millions of Americans, on top of an earlier steep increase. It adds to the problems facing the program, which the Trump administration has weakened.</article>

items.title: Trump’s Plane Flyover Is a Halloween Trick for Startled D.C. Residents
items.author: Michael Crowley
items.content: <article>A White House social media account said the surprise Air Force One flight was part of a Halloween event hosted by the president and the first lady.</article>

items.title: Why Running for the U.S. Senate Is a Rich Person’s Game
items.author: Jess Bidgood
items.content: <article>Your Senate candidates are probably richer than you.</article>

items.title: Appeals Court Again Rejects Trump Effort to Impound California Ballots
items.author: Zach Montague
items.content: <article>In a 2-to-1 vote, an appeals court panel declined to order the state to set aside more than 20,000 mail-in ballots, calling the notion plainly unconstitutional.</article>

items.title: Prosecutors Suggest They May Seek Additional Comey Charges
items.author: Devlin Barrett
items.content: <article>At a hearing in federal court, prosecutors defended an unusual, 11th-hour criminal case accusing the former F.B.I. director of leaking classified information a decade ago.</article>

items.title: Judge Appoints Special Master to Determine if Trump Officials Lied in Golf Course Suit
items.author: Zach Montague
items.content: <article>Judge Ana C. Reyes said an outside investigator would help determine whether parks officials or Justice Department lawyers withheld plans for Washington’s East Potomac Park.</article>

items.title: A Resurgent Justice Democrats Could Reshape a Democratic Congress
items.author: Catie Edmondson
items.content: <article>Justice Democrats, which gained prominence backing Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez, is on track to see more of its candidates elected. Will the party listen to them?</article>
